(frog-nmr)=
# frog-nmr

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-info}`NMR` NMR shifts, J couplings and NOE distances from ORCA outputs, with spectrum simulation.

## What it does

Turns an ORCA NMR calculation into numbers you can compare with an experimental spectrum:
chemical shifts δ (ppm), J couplings (Hz) and H···H distances with an NOE estimate, and
simulated 1D and 2D spectra (COSY, NOESY, HSQC, HMBC). Use it to assign signals, to decide
between candidate structures or diastereomers (the one whose computed shifts fit the
experiment best), or to Boltzmann-average the NMR of a conformer ensemble.

## How it works

```{include} _parts/frog-nmr/how_it_works.md
```

## Input

* An **ORCA output of an NMR calculation** on an optimised geometry: `! NMR` gives shieldings
  of all nuclei; J couplings need an `%eprnmr` block, e.g.
  `%eprnmr nuclei = all H {shift, ssall} end` (`ssall` = all spin-spin coupling terms).
  Couplings are expensive: request them only for the nuclei you need.
* A **reference** to convert shielding σ into shift δ ≈ σ_ref − σ. Best: an output of TMS (for
  1H, 13C) computed with exactly the same method, basis and solvent, passed with `--ref tms.out`.
  Without `--ref` built-in default values are used (σ_ref 31.8 ppm for 1H, 185.0 ppm for 13C).
* For `-c`: one NMR output per conformer and a checkpoint with populations (see the Ensemble
  user guide). For `--hsqc`/`--hmbc`: shieldings of both nuclei (e.g. H and C) in the same output.

### Arguments

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file` … | required | ORCA output file(s) |

**Options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-i`, `--indices` `INDICES …` |  | Show only these atoms, 0-based |
| `--shifts` |  | Show only chemical shifts |
| `--couplings` |  | Show only J couplings |
| `--distances` |  | Show only interatomic distances and NOE |
| `--save-xy` |  | Also write each simulated 1D spectrum to <stem>_1d_<nucleus>.dat |
| `--save-matrix` |  | Also write each simulated 2D spectrum to <stem>_<exp>_<f2>_<f1>.csv |

**Simulation**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--sim-1d` |  | Simulate the 1D spectrum of each nucleus (quantum spin simulation or Lorentzian lines) |
| `--sim-1d-c13` |  | Simulate the 1D 13C{1H} spectrum |
| `--cosy` |  | Simulate homonuclear COSY spectra |
| `--noesy` |  | Simulate the 1H-1H NOESY spectrum |
| `--hsqc` |  | Simulate edited HSQC / direct (1-bond) correlation spectra |
| `--hmbc` |  | Simulate HMBC / long-range correlation spectra |
| `--all-spectra` |  | Simulate all 1D and 2D spectra for all nuclei (or those given with -n) |
| `-n`, `--nuclei` `NUC …` |  | Nuclei by element or isotope (e.g. H C S or 1H 13C 33S). Restricts the tables to these elements (default: every nucleus in the output) and sets the simulated nuclei (default: 1H) |
| `--freq` `FREQ` | `500.0` | Spectrometer 1H frequency in MHz |
| `--ref` `REF …` |  | Reference shielding in ppm ('31.8', '1H=31.8,13C=185.0') or reference calculation file(s), e.g. a TMS output. A single number is applied to EVERY nucleus shown: combine it with -n, or give one value per nucleus |
| `--fwhm` `FWHM` | `1.0` | Line width (FWHM) of 1D Lorentzian lines in Hz |
| `--j-cutoff` `J_CUTOFF` | `0.3` | Minimum \|J\| in Hz for spin-cluster partitioning |
| `--r-cutoff` `R_CUTOFF` | `5.0` | Maximum distance in Å for NOE (NOESY and NOE table) |
| `--no-equiv` |  | Disable chemical-equivalence averaging |
| `--coupled` |  | Simulate all nuclei coupled (multiplets); by default only 1H is coupled |
| `--spin` `SPIN` |  | Nuclear spin of the first nucleus (e.g. '1/2', '5/2', '2.5') |
| `--spins` `SPINS` |  | Nuclear spins mapping (e.g. 'O=5/2,H=1/2' or '{"17O": 2.5}') |
| `--nuclei-file` `PATH` |  | JSON file with custom nuclear constants and spins |

**Plot options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--plot` `[PATH]` |  | Save the plot; PATH is optional |
| `--fig-format` `{png,svg,pdf,eps}` | `png` | Image format, unless the path already has an extension |
| `--dpi` `DPI` | `300` | Raster resolution of saved plots |
| `--show` |  | Also open the plot in an interactive window |
| `--title` `TEXT` |  | Plot title ('' removes it) |
| `--xlabel` `TEXT` |  | Label of the x axis |
| `--ylabel` `TEXT` |  | Label of the y axis |
| `--xlim` `MIN MAX` |  | Range of the x axis |
| `--ylim` `MIN MAX` |  | Range of the y axis |
| `--colors` `COLOR …` |  | Colours of the plotted series, in order (matplotlib names or #hex) |
| `--linewidth` `W` |  | Line width in points |
| `--linestyle` `{solid,dashed,dotted,dashdot}` |  | Line style |
| `--legend`, `--no-legend` |  | Show or hide the legend (default: decided by the plot) |
| `--grid`, `--no-grid` |  | Show or hide the grid (default: decided by the plot) |
| `--figsize` `W H` |  | Figure size in inches |
| `--font-size` `PT` |  | Base font size in points (titles and labels scale with it) |
| `--cmap` `NAME` |  | Colormap of maps and heatmaps (matplotlib or seaborn name) |

**Ensemble averaging**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-c`, `--checkpoint` `PATH` |  | Checkpoint file (checkpoint.json, or csv/json) with Boltzmann populations for ensemble averaging |
| `--read-boltzmann` `PROTOCOL` |  | Protocol whose populations are read from the checkpoint (default: protocol of each file, or the latest) |
| `-e`, `--energy-term` `{E,EZPVE,H,G}` | `G` | Energy used for on-the-fly Boltzmann weights |
| `-T`, `--temp` `TEMP` | `298.15` | Temperature in K |
| `--individual` |  | Also show per-conformer results next to the ensemble average |

**Output**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--out-dir` `DIR` |  | Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file) |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet`, `--format {table,json,csv}`, `--table-file PATH` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terminal | `Chemical Shifts & Shieldings (<file>)` | always | Per atom: σ_iso, δ (vs --ref or the default reference) and anisotropy (ppm) |
| Terminal | `Spin-Spin Couplings J (Hz) (<file>)` | always | Square J matrix (≤ 15 atoms or with -i); otherwise "Significant Spin-Spin Couplings" pair list with \|J\| ≥ 0.5 Hz and distance |
| Terminal | `Interatomic Distances (Å) (<file>)` | always | Square distance matrix (≤ 15 atoms or with -i) |
| Terminal | `NOE Estimation (<file>)` | always | Atom pairs within --r-cutoff: distance, relative NOE (∝ r⁻⁶) and intensity class |
| Terminal | `Simulated <nucleus> NMR Signals (<file>)` | `simulation flags` | Equivalence groups with σ_iso, δ and member atoms |
| Terminal | `Ensemble Weights (<n> conformers)` | `-c` | Conformer, protocol, file, Boltzmann population (%) and normalized weight (%) |
| Terminal | `... (Boltzmann average)` | `-c` | The tables above for the ensemble; distances as ⟨r⟩ and ⟨r⁻⁶⟩⁻¹ᐟ⁶ |
| File | `<stem>_1d_<nucleus>.dat` | `--save-xy` | 1D spectrum, columns ppm and intensity |
| File | `<stem>_<exp>_<f2>_<f1>.csv` | `--save-matrix` | 2D spectrum matrix; first row F2 axis, first column F1 axis (ppm) |
| Plot | `<stem>_1d_<nucleus>.png` | `--plot` | 1D spectrum of each simulated nucleus. Ensemble: nmr_ensemble_<tag> in the current directory; --plot PATH: PATH_<tag> (PATH_<stem>_<tag> for several inputs) |
| Plot | `<stem>_<exp>_<f2>_<f1>.png` | `--plot` | 2D spectra: exp = cosy, noesy, hsqc, hmbc (e.g. nmr_hsqc_1h_13c.png) |

### How to read it

* **Chemical Shifts & Shieldings**: per atom σ_iso, δ and the shielding anisotropy (ppm).
  Atom labels such as `H24` are 1-based, the *Index* column is 0-based (H24 = index 23).
  1H shifts should fall in 0–12 ppm, 13C in 0–220 ppm; with a good method and a matching TMS
  reference, typical errors are ±0.1–0.2 ppm (1H) and ±2–5 ppm (13C). A shift far outside these
  ranges usually means a wrong reference (e.g. a 1H reference applied to C or N: δ(N) = −51 ppm
  in one test) rather than a wrong structure.
* **J couplings** (Hz): a matrix for ≤ 15 atoms, otherwise a list of pairs with |J| ≥ 0.5 Hz.
  Geminal ²J(H,H) are negative (−9 to −15 Hz), vicinal ³J positive (2–12 Hz). Example
  (`NMR_ORCA.out`): CH2 pair H30/H31 −12.0 Hz, aromatic ortho pairs 6.4–6.9 Hz.
* **NOE Estimation**: pairs within 5 Å (`--r-cutoff`), relative NOE ∝ r⁻⁶ (normalised to 1.8 Å)
  and a class: Strong < 2.5 Å, Medium < 3.5 Å, Weak beyond.
* **Simulated signals**: chemically equivalent atoms (by symmetry and fast-rotating CH3) are
  merged; e.g. the methyl H37–H39 become one 3H signal at 4.248 ppm. The 1D spectrum shows
  multiplets from the full spin simulation (by default only 1H is coupled; 13C is shown
  decoupled), with the ppm axis decreasing to the right as in experiment.
* With `-c`, shifts and J are population-weighted averages and the NOE uses ⟨r⁻⁶⟩⁻¹ᐟ⁶; the
  *Ensemble Weights* table shows which file got which population.
* Warning `2D spectra are only produced with --plot or --save-matrix`: add one of the two.

## Step by step

1. Look at the data: `frog-nmr nmr.out -n H` prints the 1H shifts, the H–H J couplings and the NOE table. Without `-n` the tables contain every nucleus in the output.
2. Use a proper reference: `--ref tms.out`, or one value per nucleus `--ref 1H=31.8,13C=185.0`. A single number (`--ref 31.8`) is applied to every nucleus shown, so combine it with `-n 1H`.
3. Show only one table with `--shifts`, `--couplings` or `--distances`; `-i 23 24 25` restricts everything to those atoms (0-based) and prints full matrices.
4. Simulate spectra: `--sim-1d --plot` (1D 1H, saved as `nmr_1d_1h.png` next to the input), add `--cosy`, `--noesy`, `--hsqc`, `--hmbc` with `-n 1H 13C` for 2D maps; `--freq 400` sets the spectrometer frequency (MHz), `--save-xy`/`--save-matrix` write the data for other programs.
5. For a conformer ensemble: `frog-nmr conf_*/nmr.out -c checkpoint.json --sim-1d --plot`.

NMR shifts, J couplings and NOE distances from ORCA outputs, with spectrum simulation.

Prints shieldings/shifts, J-coupling and distance tables (with NOE estimates) for each file, or
their Boltzmann average over a conformer ensemble (-c). Simulates 1D spectra (full quantum spin
simulation for coupled nuclei, Lorentzian lines otherwise) and 2D COSY, NOESY, HSQC and HMBC
spectra for the selected nuclei (-n). Atom labels such as H5 are 1-based; -i and the Index column
are 0-based.

positional arguments:
  file                          ORCA output file(s)

options:
  -h, --help                    show this help message and exit
  -i INDICES [INDICES ...], --indices INDICES [INDICES ...]
                                Show only these atoms, 0-based
  --shifts                      Show only chemical shifts
  --couplings                   Show only J couplings
  --distances                   Show only interatomic distances and NOE
  --save-xy                     Also write each simulated 1D spectrum to <stem>_1d_<nucleus>.dat
  --save-matrix                 Also write each simulated 2D spectrum to
                                <stem>_<exp>_<f2>_<f1>.csv

simulation:
  --sim-1d                      Simulate the 1D spectrum of each nucleus (quantum spin simulation
                                or Lorentzian lines)
  --sim-1d-c13                  Simulate the 1D 13C{1H} spectrum
  --cosy                        Simulate homonuclear COSY spectra
  --noesy                       Simulate the 1H-1H NOESY spectrum
  --hsqc                        Simulate edited HSQC / direct (1-bond) correlation spectra
  --hmbc                        Simulate HMBC / long-range correlation spectra
  --all-spectra                 Simulate all 1D and 2D spectra for all nuclei (or those given with
                                -n)

                                Nuclei by element or isotope (e.g. H C S or 1H 13C 33S). Restricts
